---
title: "Baby Names"
format: html
execute:
  echo: true
---

## Loading the Data

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)

# Find all yearly data files
files <- list.files("data", pattern = "yob\\d+\\.txt", full.names = TRUE)

# Read all files into one table and extract the year from the filename
baby_names <- read_csv(
  files,
  id = "file",
  col_names = c("name", "sex", "count"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  mutate(year = parse_number(file)) |>
  select(-file)
```

## Trend of "David" (Past 100 Years)

```{r}
#| label: david-trend

david_100yr <- baby_names |>
  filter(name == "David", year >= 1926) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarize(total = sum(count), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(david_100yr, aes(x = year, y = total)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Number of Babies Named David (1926–2025)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Over the past 100 years (1926–2025), the name David surged during the baby boom era, peaking in 1955 with 86,454 babies, before steadily declining to 6,801 in 2025.
